thesis: A net-cash pharma with rising returns and margins trades low in its own EV/EBITDA and P/FCF ranges while in a healthy uptrend.
reason: Scorecard gives conviction 4: high, rising returns, net cash, and trend strength with a real FCF yield. Python sets the volatility-scaled size; cash after the pending order cannot fund it above the 1.5% floor, so the conviction-3 OTIS holding is sold to fund it.

triggers.text: TTM operating margin falls below 28%, reversing most of the rise from 28.7% a year earlier to 34.5%.
TTM ROIC falls below 16%, back to the FY2021 level and erasing the returns improvement.
TTM FCF margin falls below 18%, showing the rolling slide from 29.3% is structural, not timing.
Net debt/EBITDA (ratios page) rises above 1.0x from -0.61x, signalling a debt-funded deal.

replacement_reason: OTIS is held at conviction 3 with its price above the mechanical fair value and a balanced skew (its own thesis); Richter clears the buy bar with higher returns, net cash and a lower EV/EBITDA, and cash cannot fund a full position above the 1.5% floor.
